//: VITE RESOLVES A TSCONFIG PER FILE AND THE NEAREST ONE WINS, WHICH IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM. apps/admin/tsconfig.json sets `jsx: preserve` under ADR-095 F7, and that is correct for the application: nothing here is built by `tsc`, so Next emits and `tsc --noEmit` only reads. VITEST HAS NO BUNDLER BEHIND IT, so preserved JSX reaches the import analyser as invalid syntax and the suite fails to load before one assertion runs, with Vite naming the cause itself: `Failed to parse source for import analysis because the content contains invalid JS syntax. If you use tsconfig.json, make sure to not set jsx to preserve.` This file overrides `jsx` for THIS DIRECTORY ONLY, so the app keeps the setting its build needs and test/render.test.ts gets JavaScript. apps/portal/src/app/calendar/tsconfig.json is the precedent and it was measured there rather than here: an `esbuild` block in vitest.config.ts was tried and does not work, because Vite reads the per-file tsconfig in preference. `tsc` never reads this file, because it compiles the project it is pointed at, and Next never reads it either.
